# ruststream-sqlx

> `ruststream-sqlx` brings SQL databases into RustStream, a Rust framework for services that subscribe to message brokers and publish to them, through `sqlx`: a transactional outbox over any RustStream broker, and task queues in Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables.

This site holds the entry pages. The crate is documented item by item on docs.rs, and the framework itself on the RustStream site.

## Site

- [Home](https://powersemmi.github.io/ruststream-sqlx/latest/): the two components and where the rest of the documentation is

## Guides

- [The inbox broker](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-inbox-broker): task queues in the service's Postgres, MySQL/MariaDB and SQLite tables, taken by row lock or by lease; what each handler outcome does to a row, and where "now" comes from
- [Row locks or leases](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#row-locks-or-leases): the two forms a queue table takes its rows in, what each holds while a handler runs, and when to declare `#[field(locked_until)]`
- [The lease form](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#the-lease-form): the claim that commits, the lease as the ownership token, its extension every half lease, `LeaseLost`, and attempts counted at the claim
- [Databases](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#databases): what Postgres, MySQL 8.0.1 and MariaDB 10.6, SQLite and an `AnyPool` each serve, and a dialect of the service's own
- [Startup checks and rows that do not decode](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#startup-checks-and-rows-that-do-not-decode): what stops a subscription when it opens, and the decode-failure policy that settles a row whose columns do not decode
- [Batches](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#batches): one claim as a batch, settled together in the row lock form and row by row in the lease form
- [Routes and by-name subscriptions](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#routes-and-by-name-subscriptions): publishing into tables through repositories and routes, `#[subscriber("name")]`, and what each costs per message
- [Testing a service on the inbox](https://docs.rs/ruststream-sqlx/latest/ruststream_sqlx/index.html#testing-a-service-on-the-inbox): `TestApp::start_live` against a real database or an in-memory SQLite, and the real clock
